lesson.subtitle: Lesson 6 -- Money, Prices and Shopping
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Thiago Negrães | Lesson 6 -- Money, Prices and Shopping

vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: Money taken off the normal price
How much of one currency you get for another
To have enough money for something
The percentage added at the till, on top of the price on the label
A fixed amount a company charges for a service
Something that costs much less than it is worth
The paper that proves what you paid
The promise to repair or replace a product for a period of time

vocab.text: Two words a Brazilian never expects. In the United States the price on the label is not the price you pay: sales tax is added at the till and it changes from state to state. And a fee is not a tax: it is what the company itself charges you, and it is often the difference between two offers that look identical.

reading.rtitle: Two Ways to Buy the Same Laptop
paras: The same laptop sits in two windows on the same street. The store on the corner asks nine hundred dollars and calls it a bargain. The one across the road asks eight hundred and fifty, which looks cheaper, and most people stop reading there. They should not. The label price in the United States is never the final price, because sales tax is added at the till, and the two stores are in different counties with different rates.

Then come the parts nobody compares. The first store includes a three-year warranty; the second sells one for a hundred and twenty dollars, and charges a restocking fee of fifteen per cent if you bring the machine back. Pay with a Brazilian card and the exchange rate on the day adds its own difference, plus a fee from the bank. The cheapest offer is almost never the smallest number on the window. It is the one you can still afford after you have read everything, and the receipt is what proves which one you really took.

reading.prompt: What is the best title for this text?
choices: Why laptops are more expensive in the United States
Why the lowest label price is often not the cheapest offer
How to choose between two laptop brands

items: The price on the label is the price you pay in the United States.
The text says sales tax is added at the till, so the label price is never the final price.
The second store charges extra if you bring the machine back.
The text says it charges a restocking fee of fifteen per cent.
The two stores pay the same sales tax rate.
The text says they are in different counties with different rates.
You are holding two offers for the same product. Explain to a colleague which one is better and why.
The price at the till is higher than the price on the label. Ask the clerk what happened.
You want the item but not at this price. Ask whether there is any discount.

practice.title: Turn each cue into a full sentence. Use the structure in brackets.
items: The second plan / the first one.
This option / on the whole list.

items.situation: The total at the till is higher than the number you read on the label.
tips: One word explains the difference, and it is added at the end.
Ask politely why the total is different.

items.situation: You are comparing two offers and one includes three years of repairs.
tips: The promise to repair has a name.
Compare the two with a comparative, not with two separate sentences.

items.situation: The product is good but the price is above what you planned to spend.
tips: There is a verb for having enough money.
Ask whether there is any reduction.

items.situation: You are paying with a Brazilian card and you want to know the real cost.
tips: Two things change the number: one is the rate, the other is what the bank charges.
Ask about both in one question.

items.situation: A colleague asks which of the three offers you would take.
tips: A superlative decides it in one sentence.

answerkey.title: Reveal the model answers
list: The second plan is cheaper than the first one.
This option is the most expensive on the whole list.
The exchange rate is better today than it was yesterday.
That is the worst deal in the store.
answerkey.note: These are models, not the only correct answers. Any natural sentence with the right comparative or superlative works.

listenings.text: Good afternoon, shoppers. Here are today's offers. All winter coats are thirty per cent off until closing time, which makes them cheaper than anything on our website. Remember that the price on the label does not include sales tax. Our two-year warranty is free with every laptop this week, and the extended one is the cheapest it has been all year. Keep your receipt: without it we cannot exchange anything after seven days. And there is no fee if you return an item in the same week.

This is your card provider with a short message about spending abroad. When you pay in dollars, we use the exchange rate of the day, and we add a fee of two per cent on every international purchase. Paying in the local currency is almost always better than letting the shop convert the amount for you, because the shop's rate is usually the worst one available. If you cannot afford a large purchase in one payment, call us before you travel and we will look at the options together.

extra_audio.text: First, Thiago found the same laptop in two stores on the same street. Then he compared the two labels and saw that one was fifty dollars cheaper. After that, he read the small print and found the restocking fee. Next, he asked the clerk about the warranty and the sales tax. Finally, he bought the more expensive one, because it was the better deal, and he kept the receipt.
